## Key Terms

**Excel date.** A date stored in a workbook as a number, a count of days, which Excel displays as a date because of the cell's format. In the 1900 date system of CharlesRiver.xlsx, 1 is January 1, 1900. A program that reads the workbook can receive the number instead of the date, as Power Query Online did in Guided Tutorial C.1, so a date column's type is checked as well as its values.

**Model editor.** The part of the Power BI service that opens a semantic model in a browser to view it or, in Editing mode, to change it: its relationships, measures, calculated tables, properties, and roles. Changes made in Editing mode are saved as they are made, with no undo.

**My workspace.** A user's personal area in the Power BI service, where even a free license can create semantic models and reports for the user's own use. Sharing its content with others needs a paid license, such as Pro.

**Power BI service.** The website at app.powerbi.com where Power BI reports are published, shared, and read in a browser, and where dashboards are built. It also builds semantic models with Power Query Online and edits them in the model editor, so much of the work of Power BI Desktop can be done in a browser, with some commands in other places and a few features missing.

**Power Query Online.** The browser version of the Power Query Editor, used by the Power BI service and other Microsoft services to get and shape data. It offers the transformations of the editor in Excel and Power BI Desktop, though its connectors, its sign-in, and some of its commands and step names differ.

**Tenant setting.** A setting that an organization's Power BI administrator controls for all its users or for some of them, such as whether users can edit semantic models in the browser. A feature turned off in the tenant settings is unavailable whatever the user's license.

**Version history.** The last few saved versions of a semantic model edited in the Power BI service, each of which can be restored. It needs a Pro license and permission to edit the model, keeps up to five versions with their data, supports restoring a version only up to 14 days old, and is not a substitute for version control.
